column1: # derivation: COALESCE(a, ..., z) is built as CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN
# a ... ELSE z (§8.14: "COALESCE, which is a CASE"); by §1.7 that CASE takes
# the first WHEN whose condition is TRUE, so it answers its first non-NULL
# argument, and the last argument (NULL) when every argument is NULL (§1.3:
# IS NOT NULL is never NULL). Over int_pairs (x, y) =
# 20, 3, NULL, 5; COALESCE(y, x) is 10, 20, 3, NULL, 5; COALESCE(x, y, 0)
# is 1, 20, 3, 0, 5. Types: x, y and the literal 0 are INT64 (§8.19), so
# each COALESCE is INT64; nullable (§8), the 0-terminated one included.
